admission_apply.text: Only ivory, and one lost tooth. The bead may be a trick of the polish.

native.admission_inspect: A slim ivory comb. One tooth is gone. A still bead sits in the gap, and the ivory is dry.
apply_texts: A second pass finds the bead seated, as though the wipe had never happened.
Again the bead. It should have broken on the tooth beside it. It only shifts.
Cold runs the comb. The bead swells by a breath, then is the same size again.
For a breath the gap is only a gap, and the bead is only water.
Only ivory, and one lost tooth. The bead may be a trick of the polish.
The bead draws itself into a bright line and stops short of a shape.
The line almost becomes a word. You set the comb down before it can.
The water is in the gap again, small and exact, with no source you can see.
You draw the comb once. The bead rides the gap and leaves no damp behind.
inspect_texts: A pale line of water fills the missing tooth, then thins before it can mean anything.
A slim ivory comb. One tooth is gone. A still bead sits in the gap, and the ivory is dry.
Cold climbs the teeth. The absent one keeps a bead that will not fall or wet you.
One tooth is gone. The bead there is thin as a silk thread, and the ivory is dry.
The gap was wiped. The bead has returned, no larger, and your thumb is still dry.
The ivory is cold as a cup left out. One tooth is missing, and the gap looks wet.
The same bead, or a twin of it. It holds the light and gives none back.
The wet gap nearly makes a letter, then fails, and you cannot say which letter.
native.name: Seamwater Comb
